title: Octopus-Rex_Botnet_Investigation_c69
description: Investigate and contain the Octopus-Rex botnet infection on compromised systems within the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Octopus-Rex botnet is a multi-task botnet capable of various malicious activities including command and control (C2) communication, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. Your task is to investigate and contain this botnet infection on compromised systems within the network.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the bot1 host:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service responsible for beaconing activity?
levels.solution: Check running services and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is likely named 'bot-beacon.service'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for unusual network connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services related to network communication and periodic tasks.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The service name likely contains 'bot' and describes its function. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

levels.title: Identify Flood Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating the flood attack traffic?
levels.solution: Investigate systemd timers and services for unusual network activity. The service generating the flood attack traffic is likely named 'bot-flood.service'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers and services for unusual network activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services related to network flooding and periodic tasks.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The service name likely contains 'bot' and describes its function. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Examine systemd timers and services for clues about automatic startup. The persistence mechanism is likely named 'system-update-checker.timer'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine systemd timers and services for clues about automatic startup.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers related to system updates or health checks.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The timer name likely contains 'checker' and describes its function. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.
